newsitem.title: USA: Dlr jolted by Dow slide, Buba rate fears at US end.
newsitem.headline: Dlr jolted by Dow slide, Buba rate fears at US end.

text.p: Dollar/mark ended sharply lower on Friday, hurt by a sharp fall in U.S. stocks and mounting speculation that Germany will raise interest rates.
Dollar/yen also fell from early highs but a robust mark/yen and concerns about the yen's exposure to recent Southeast Asian currency devaluations slowed the decline.
The dollar fell about two pfennigs, hitting a low of 1.8155, as investors liquidated dollars and dollar-denominated investments, fearing the recent bull-run has come to an end.
"The worm has turned, so to speak," said John Barlow, senior dealer at Bayerishe Landesbank Girzentrale in New York.
"The tough talk from the Bundesbank and the slightly overbought situation in the dollar and oversold situation in the mark has created a new outlook."
The dollar closed at 1.8185/95 marks, down from 1.8355/59 at the open. It ended at 117.39/44 yen, off from 118.42/52.
The German central bank has been sounding warnings about inflation all week and alarm bells were still ringing through the market on Friday.
On Thursday hawkish remarks from Bundesbank vice president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum fanned expectations that it might boost short term interest rates when it returns from summer recess next Thursday.
Hedge funds reportedly sold dollar/mark when it broke below support at Wednesday's 1.8280 low, where stop-loss sell orders had accumulated.
The dollar got little support from European markets, many of which were closed in observance of a religious holiday, Assumption Day.

"There is a whole lot going on here. I think the asset markets taking a dive certainly have not helped. A big holiday in Europe and thin markets certainly exaggerated the move," said Cynthia Cooley, a senior trader at United Gulf Bank of Bahrain in Boston.
The Dow industrials tumbled 247 points ending at 7695. The 30-year Treasury bond ended flat after trimming early losses of about a point.
Against the yen, the dollar reversed overnight gains but garnered some support amid yen weakness against the mark in the wake of Indonesia's devaluation of the rupiah Thursday.
Mark/yen remained well underpinned near 64.50, just under the 64.65 day's high, for most of the session. Sterling/yen also ended firmly, but off its highs, around 189.
Indonesia floated the rupiah under pressure from speculators, following similar actions by several neighboring countries in recent weeks. The currency hit another record low on Friday.
Traders feared Japan might be compelled to weaken the yen to keep its exports competitive with other Pacific rim nations.
"With dollar/yen, I think it hasn't come off quite as much because of turbulence in the region, which probably engenders some interest in the mark/yen cross as well," Cooley said.
"Some would argue that the yen could become a regional safe haven currency but I think it's more likely that we'll see it weighs on the region as a whole," she added.
In other trade, the dollar fell to 1.5030/40 Swiss francs from 1.5150/60 at the open but rose to Canadian $1.3905/10 from C$1.3890/95.
The pound rose to $1.6090/00 from $1.5992/02 and the Australian dollar rose to $0.7420/25 from $0.7410/15.
((-- Alden Bentley, 212 859 1667))
